 - (2) [dbt-labs/dbt-core #12862](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/12862) CONFIRMED OPEN — title: '[Bug] Trino/Starburst Cannot use grants with roles. #12862'. Core problem: dbt-trino adapter generates `GRANT SELECT ON table TO ""` (bare-name form) instead of `GRANT SELECT ON table TO ROLE <name>` that Trino/Starburst expects. Labeled bug + triage, no assignee. The #12862 detail IS CONFIRMED — kept as the hard claim (no softening needed).
 - (3) [trino.io/docs/current/sql/grant.html](https://trino.io/docs/current/sql/grant.html) — Trino GRANT grammar: `GRANT ( privilege [, ...] | ( ALL PRIVILEGES ) ) ON [ BRANCH branch_name IN ] ( table_name | TABLE table_name | SCHEMA schema_name) TO ( user | USER user | ROLE role )`. The grantee is one of THREE alternatives: bare `user` (defaults to USER), `USER user`, or `ROLE role`. The bare-name form interprets the grantee as a USER per Trino's principal-resolution defaults — so omitting `ROLE` when granting to a role produces a wrong-principal grant. NOTE: the `ROLE` keyword is not strictly grammar-required (the bare form parses) — but it IS required semantically to grant to a role rather than a same-named user. Phrased the canonical accordingly: 'omit the ROLE keyword and the bare name resolves to a USER, so for a role grantee write TO ROLE <role> explicitly' (instead of asserting 'ROLE keyword is grammar-required' which would be false per the syntax block).
